title: Tree Habitat
subtitle: A speculative vertical community beside Shenzhen's mangrove coast
overview: Tree Habitat is a speculative vertical community for Shenzhen's mobile working population. Set beside the mangrove coast of the Greater Bay Area, the tower combines office, public culture, commerce, hotel programs and sky gardens into one climate-responsive high-rise structure. Its root-like base, three tower bodies and layered green platforms translate mangrove ecology into an urban habitat organized around working, gathering and staying near the city center.
storyHtml:
Shenzhen is built on movement. Many people come for work, but the city center that concentrates opportunity often separates work from daily life. Tree Habitat proposes a vertical alternative: production, leisure and public functions are compressed into one active urban organism.

The project takes its structural imagination from the mangrove reserve across the road. Mangroves do not stand as isolated objects. Their roots interlock, stabilize unstable ground and create a shared habitat. In the tower, this logic becomes a split root base for traffic and public programs, a dense trunk for office and company space, three tower bodies as branches, and high-level gardens as leaves.

Circulation is treated as ecology rather than only transport. Express elevators, local elevators, transfer levels and bridged commercial floors separate different user groups while allowing them to meet where programs overlap. Public culture, retail and sky clubs occupy the lower and middle zones; hotel, restaurants and observation spaces rise above.

A double facade, vertical gardens, heat chimney and geothermal system moderate the tower's climate. The building grows, breathes and circulates like a small city, turning the high-rise from an isolated object into a working habitat.
